subject: Re: Model fit + quantization trade study — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + recommended next steps (model fit / quantization)

Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call plus recommended next steps so we have a single plan to move to an eval: 

Summary of needs from FinApps:
- Low-latency generation for customer-facing chat (95th pctl latency target: ~300ms)
- High throughput for batch enrichment (embedding + reranking) during nightly jobs
- Strong instruction-following & extraction for financial document summarization
- Tight quality budget: <1.5% critical regression on our eval set vs current in-house baseline

Model recommendations (initial):
- Candidate A: Redwood-Instruct-13B (good quality/cost balance)
- Candidate B: Mistral-Instruct-7B (fast, lower cost; watch hallucination on long docs)
- Candidate C: Llama-2-70B-chat / 70B quantized variant (best raw quality; higher compute)

Quantization / throughput options to evaluate (high level):
- AWQ (8-bit asymmetric with fine-tuned quant matrices): best throughput gains for 13B/70B while often preserving quality on instruction tasks; low inference-time memory.
- GPTQ (4/3-bit style per-tensor): highest memory reduction but quality can degrade for some prompt patterns, needs per-layer tuning.
- FP8 / mixed-precision kernels: lower latency on next-gen GPUs (H100/A100) but availability depends on infra; usually safest for quality but less compression than GPTQ.

Attachments I will share after this: baseline eval CSV, tradeoffs PDF, and the prompt set we used.

Next steps / proposed action items:
1) Redwood to run a targeted eval across the three candidate models + AWQ + GPTQ options using your prompt set (we'll port your sample prompts). (owner: Marissa)
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer to align on latency SLO and deployment constraints. (owner: Dylan)
3) Share initial quantized tradeoff summary and a recommended production configuration. (owner: Marissa / Dylan)

Are you OK with the proposed candidates and plan? If so we'll kick off the eval this week and target a re-cap by Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap + recommended next steps (model fit / quantization)

Alex — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers and what we'll include in the one-pager / eval deliverable: 

1) Expected perf (ballpark / per-token) on your infra
- Redwood-Instruct-13B:
  - FP16 baseline (T4): ~20-30 tokens/sec (per-card), 95th pctl latency ~280-450ms depending on seq len
  - AWQ (8-bit): ~35-45 tokens/sec, 95th pctl latency ~220-350ms — very good quality retention on instruction tasks
  - GPTQ (4-bit aggressive): ~60-80 tokens/sec memory-wise but we often see edge-case regressions on structured extraction prompts
- Mistral-7B-Instruct:
  - FP16: ~45-70 tokens/sec, AWQ: ~70-100 tokens/sec, GPTQ: ~120+ tokens/sec but watch long-context stability
- Llama-2-70B-chat:
  - FP16 (H100): ~120-200 tokens/sec; AWQ/GPTQ on 70B brings meaningful throughput but requires careful per-layer calibration and validation

Notes: these are rough estimates from our internal benchmarking on T4/H100 variants. We'll run the exact configs against your provided prompts and hardware targets.

2) Prompt set sampling
We'll run the full prompt set you shared but with stratified reporting: 
- Short convo prompts (user chat)
- Long-doc summarization / extraction (legal/financial)
- Edge-case structured extraction (tables, dates, totals)

3) Tradeoffs (ops & rollback risk) we'll document in the one-pager- AWQ: low operational risk, straightforward rollback to FP16, fast perf gains
- GPTQ: highest compression, harder rollback (requires model re-quantization to revert), may require per-layer/ln tuning; higher QA time
- FP8/mixed-precision: safest for quality on new GPU types but less compression than GPTQ; depends on runtime kernel support

Deliverables we will send after the run (ETA: 48-72 hours):
- finapps_eval_results.csv (per-prompt metrics: ROUGE/F1/QA accuracy + latency/throughput columns)
- quantization_tradeoffs.pdf (one-pager + tables showing where quality regresses occur)
- prompt_set_v1.txt (the exact prompts used)
- quick annotated notebook link (Drive) with config snippets to reproduce locally

I've attached the initial prompt set and will upload the evaluation artifacts once the run completes. We will flag any prompts where AWQ/GPTQ cause >1.5% critical regression.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alex — Dylan here (solutions engineering). Thanks for the quick answers, Alex. Two logistical items from our side before we start the production-like runs: 

1) Can you confirm the exact GCP instance types you want us to emulate (T4: n1-standard-16 + 1xT4 vs H100: a2-highgpu-1g or similar)? We want to match batch sizes and tokenization pipeline.
2) For long-doc jobs, do you want us to evaluate chunking + KV-cache (recommended) vs single-stream long-context? We typically recommend KV-cache + chunking to preserve quantized-model stability on very long docs.

Proposed times: 60-min deep-dive Monday 2026-03-23 09:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite if that works for your infra/ML engineer. During the call we can review the CSV and the exact prompts that triggered regressions (if any).

Action items assigned:
